summary: A model server on loopback - llama.cpp, llama-swap, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, anything that speaks /v1/chat/completions. Nothing leaves the machine.

requires.name: local OpenAI-compatible server
requires.description: Anything serving GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions on loopback.
requires.howTo: llama.cpp: `llama-server -m model.gguf -c 65536 --port 8888`. llama-swap: point its config at your GGUFs. Ollama: serves on 11434, prefix ids with the model name. LM Studio: enable the local server in Developer settings.

requires.name: PI_LOCAL_BASE_URL
requires.description: Overrides the base URL extensions/credentials.ts registers for the `local` provider. REQUIRED whenever the port is not 8888 - see the notes: the extension's baseUrl wins over models.json.
requires.howTo: The installer writes `export PI_LOCAL_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1"` into config/shell/pi-env.sh from the port answer below.

requires.name: LOCAL_API_KEY
requires.description: Only if your server (or the backend it proxies to) checks a bearer token. Most loopback servers do not.
requires.howTo: Export it from your shell profile; reference it below as $LOCAL_API_KEY rather than pasting the value.

prompts.label: Port your local server listens on
prompts.help: 8888 is what extensions/credentials.ts assumes when PI_LOCAL_BASE_URL is unset. Any other value obliges the installer to export PI_LOCAL_BASE_URL as well - see the notes.

prompts.label: API key reference for the local server
prompts.help: Leave the default unless your server checks a token. `$LOCAL_API_KEY` reads the environment variable; a literal string is sent as-is. It must NOT be empty - see the notes.

prompts.label: Context window your server was STARTED with
prompts.help: The -c / --ctx-size the server is running with, not the model's native window. PI's compaction trusts this number; set it too high and the server truncates silently.

models.name: [local] EXAMPLE - thinking toggled through a chat-template kwarg

notes: THE THREE MODELS ABOVE ARE EXAMPLES AND WILL NOT WORK UNSELECTED. Replace `id` with the exact string your server returns from GET /v1/models - `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/models | jq -r '.data[].id'`. For llama.cpp that is usually the model filename; for llama-swap the alias in its config; for Ollama the `name:tag`. `name` is only the label shown in /model, so keep the `[local]` prefix if you like it.

ADDING MORE MODELS. Append another object to `providers.local.models` in config/models.json. The three shapes above cover the three cases worth knowing: always-thinking, thinking toggled by a chat-template kwarg, and non-thinking. Copy the closest one.

THE compat BLOCK IS THE PART THAT IS HARD TO REDISCOVER. Each flag maps to exactly one observed failure. supportsDeveloperRole:false - 400 on every request complaining about role `developer`. supportsReasoningEffort:false - 400 on reasoning_effort, which llama.cpp does not model. supportsUsageInStreaming:false - 400 on stream_options, or no usage at end of stream. maxTokensField:max_tokens - 400 on max_completion_tokens. supportsFinishReason:false is the worst one to get wrong: the server omits finish_reason, the turn never ends and PI waits forever; `false` makes PI infer stop/toolUse when the stream closes. Rule of thumb for any new endpoint: start with everything off and max_tokens, get one successful turn, then enable one capability at a time. Turning a flag off that was needed costs a feature; turning one on that is unsupported costs a 400 on every request.

thinkingFormat AND samplingParams ARE PER-MODEL, NOT PER-PROVIDER. `thinkingFormat: "qwen-chat-template"` on Qwen-family GGUFs: the thinking toggle is a chat-template kwarg, not an API parameter, and without this the toggle is silently ignored. `thinkingFormat: "chat-template"` plus chatTemplateKwargs is the general form - the {"$var": "thinking.enabled"} / {"$var": "thinking.effort"} indirection lets PI's own thinking level drive whatever kwarg the template expects (e.g. reasoning_effort for harmony-format models). samplingParams carries min_p / top_k / repeat_penalty / presence_penalty, which have no first-class PI fields and are merged verbatim into the request body; use the values the model card publishes, because a thinking model at the wrong temperature degrades in ways that look like a harness bug.

thinkingLevelMap DESCRIBES WHAT THE MODEL CAN BE STEERED TO, NOT WHAT THE SERVER ACCEPTS. Both thinking examples above carry a BOOLEAN on the wire - `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking = !!reasoningEffort` - so `low` and `max` are the same request, and the map nulls minimal/low/medium/xhigh/max to leave exactly `off` and `high`: thinking-off versus thinking-on, with any requested level clamping onto one of the two. Do not widen this because a curl succeeded: an OpenAI-compatible server will happily 200 on every value of reasoning_effort it recognises while the provider never transmits one (`compat.supportsReasoningEffort` is false here). A model that genuinely carries a graded level - a harmony-format model with `chatTemplateKwargs: {"reasoning_effort": {"$var": "thinking.effort"}}` - should instead have NO map at all, since an absent map already reads as off/minimal/low/medium/high supported and xhigh/max not. A model whose template ignores thinking entirely gets an all-null map, which is a statement about steerability and not about whether it reasons.

contextWindow MUST EQUAL WHAT THE SERVER WAS LAUNCHED WITH. Not the model's native window. PI's compaction trusts this number; set it high and the server truncates the prompt silently, which presents as the agent forgetting things mid-task.

apiKey MUST BE PRESENT AND MUST RESOLVE, EVEN IF YOUR SERVER IGNORES IT. With no key in either layer PI's apiKey auth resolves to undefined, reads the provider as unconfigured, and its models never reach /model or --list-models - which looks like the harness being broken. With an unresolvable $VAR the same thing happens. Hence the `not-required` default: a literal, non-secret, obviously-inert string. Anything non-empty works.

AUTH BELONGS TO WHATEVER THE ROUTER ROUTES TO, NOT TO THE ROUTER. This cost three attempts to pin down and is the finding worth keeping. If you run a router (llama-swap and friends), its own GET /v1/models is typically open and enforces nothing, and a model served by a bare llama.cpp behind it will answer a completion with any header or none. Probe either and the port reads as keyless. A different model behind the SAME port may be served by a backend that does require a bearer token, and it will 401 on the first real completion. Which model you sample decides the answer, so one model proves nothing about the port.

THE WARM-UP PING IS WORTH EXACTLY WHAT IT MEASURES. extensions/credentials.ts sends an unauthenticated GET /v1/models with a 3 s budget at session start. It proves the router is up and answering. It does NOT prove a model is loaded, that a completion will succeed, or anything at all about the key. A wrong key surfaces on the first real completion as a fail-loud abort naming the provider.

DO NOT SET apiKey IN AN EXTENSION AS WELL. PI's provider composer resolves `extension?.apiKey ?? config?.apiKey`, so an extension-declared key WINS over models.json and two files end up obliged to agree about a value only one of them owns. extensions/credentials.ts deliberately declares baseUrl, api and refreshModels only.

concurrency IS 1 ON PURPOSE. One machine holds one model at a time and a router unloads on switch; parallel dispatch onto a local model thrashes. This is a semaphore in the dispatcher, keyed on the resolved provider id - it queues rather than errors.

TOOL-CALL QUALITY IS THE REAL LIMIT. A small local model emits malformed tool JSON at a materially higher rate than a frontier model, and PI exposes no repair-retry knob. Keep local off the main loop; bind it to the `local` tier and use it for cheap sub-agent work.

models.json's baseUrl DOES NOT WIN FOR THIS PROVIDER. PI's provider composer resolves `extension?.baseUrl ?? config?.baseUrl ?? base?.baseUrl`, and extensions/credentials.ts re-registers `local` with `localBaseUrl()`, which is `process.env.PI_LOCAL_BASE_URL ?? "http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1"`. So on any port other than 8888 the installer MUST also export PI_LOCAL_BASE_URL in config/shell/pi-env.sh, or requests go to 8888 while models.json innocently says otherwise. Keep the two in agreement; the baseUrl written into models.json is what a human reads and what the provider falls back to if the extension is ever removed.

NO `cost` MEANS THE STATUS LINE READS 0.000, NOT THAT IT HIDES THE FIGURE. `cost` is optional in this file and required on PI's runtime model type, and the provider composer fills the gap with {input:0,output:0,cacheRead:0,cacheWrite:0} rather than refusing - so every session on a provider defined here displays a flat zero spend, silently, whatever the calls really cost. For a server holding local weights that zero is the honest number: nothing is metered and no invoice exists, and the real price of this lane is wall-clock time, RAM and battery, none of which the cost object can express. It stops being honest the moment the port fronts something remote - a router proxying a paid API bills exactly as that API does. Units, if you do fill it in: DOLLARS PER MILLION TOKENS, because PI divides each rate by 1000000 before multiplying by the usage counter. Getting that wrong by six orders of magnitude looks like a working status line.

NO TIMEOUT FIELDS EXIST IN PI'S PROVIDER SCHEMA. A cold start that has to page tens of GB of weights can exceed PI's default HTTP timeout. That is why extensions/credentials.ts re-registers this provider with its own AbortSignal budget and the warm-up ping. Re-registering a CUSTOM provider is safe; re-registering a built-in one (github-copilot, openai, anthropic) would destroy its auth block.
